card.title: Conservation of mechanical energy
card.body: $E_1 = E_2 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad E_{k1} + E_{p1} + E_{ps1} = E_{k2} + E_{p2} + E_{ps2}$
card.says: when only conservative forces (gravity and ideal springs) do work, total mechanical energy $E = E_k + E_p + E_{ps}$ stays **constant** and only changes form. If a non-conservative force such as friction does work $W_{\text{nc}}$, then $E_1 + W_{\text{nc}} = E_2$.
card.from: the work-energy theorem, separating net work into conservative work ($-\Delta E_p - \Delta E_{ps}$) and non-conservative work ($W_{\text{nc}} = 0$ when friction and air drag are absent).
card.useWhen: you want a speed, height, or spring compression between two positions—especially on curved tracks or ramps where forces keep changing direction.
card.example: Sliding from rest down a frictionless $h = 2.5\text{ m}$ slide (with $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$): $m g h = \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2 \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 2.5} = \sqrt{49} = 7\text{ m/s}$, regardless of mass.
card.analogy: Pouring water back and forth between two cups without spilling: the amount in each cup changes, but the total water never does.
